column1: # THE 10-YEAR LEG's record bands (2026-10-05, the bond-fund consumer's request): the two rows of
# `bond10_readings` / `bond10Readings` on FRED's DGS10 constant-maturity yield read as a 10-year par
# bond rebought every observation (the coupon accrues over the calendar days held, the price moves
# with the yield, semiannual compounding; `record_bands -yahoo DGS10.csv` reads the series), the
# record both sets grade the leg (`-bond10`, duration 8 at the sets' dials) against:
#   bond10 vol per duration  the annualised RMS of each session's log return over the par bond's
#                         modified duration at the prior yield, percent per year of duration: the
#                         record's duration runs from about 6 (1981) to 9 (2020), so dividing session
#                         by session keeps it out of the row; the model reads its leg's RMS over the
#                         leg's own duration, so the duration the verdict runs it at does not move it
#   bond10 depth vs vol   the share of sessions more than 10% under the running peak over what the
#                         volatility implies (`0.0397 x vol - 0.0785`), the bond row's reading
#   bond10 excess return pts/yr  each session's log return less DFF's log accrual over the same
#                         calendar days (actual/365), averaged and taken to a year at the window's
#                         own 249.76 sessions a year: the term premium's row.  The window starts
#                         and ends near a 4% 10-year yield, so the 1966-81 losses and the 1981-2020
#                         gains roughly cancel and the realised excess estimates the average premium;
#                         its sampling spread is about 1.3 points either side
# Each row carries the record's reading and its spread over 20,000 moving one-year-block resamples;
# the three rows share their own joint band (`-of 3`, alpha 0.10), outside the equity window's.
# `Anchors.bond10_window` / `bond10_years` (64) are this window; the model reads the leg at that
# horizon. FRED's DGS10 is public domain; the 1962-01-03..2026-08-03 window is the one the TLT bond
# row ends on.
# Generated by `rust/src/bin/record_bands.rs -bond10` (twin: `jsrc/recordBands.sc -bond10`):
#   record_bands -bond10 -set sp500|nasdaq -series DGS10 -yahoo <FRED DGS10> -fred <FRED DFF>
